exposure: more than four antenatal care visits
cohort: The study included 37,140 newborns and their mothers from five East African countries whose data were collected between 2019 and 2023.
finding: The study found a low prevalence of mother-newborn skin-to-skin contact in East African countries, with immediate breastfeeding, primary education, and more than four antenatal care visits being positive predictors, while multiple births, cesarean section, and rural residence were negative predictors.
mod_finding: Cesarean section deliveries were significantly associated with a lower likelihood of receiving skin-to-skin contact (AOR = 0.26).
country: Kenya, Mozambique, Tanzania, Rwanda, Madagascar (representing East Africa)
birth_weight: Measured as an exposure (low birth weight)
